requirements.text: A subject gets the same variant for an experiment on every visit and device that shares its id
Variant weights are honored, and a zero-weight variant is never assigned
Assignments in different experiments are independent (hashing is salted by the experiment)
An exposure event is recorded once per subject when the variant is actually shown
A subject keeps its variant when an anonymous visitor signs in
Changing traffic allocation does not silently reassign subjects already in the experiment
Conversion metrics are attributed per variant with a statistical significance check

evidence.name: deterministic assignment: a subject gets the same variant on every visit and on every instance sharing its id
weighted variants: weights are honored and a zero-weight variant is never assigned
experiment independence: assignments in two experiments are uncorrelated because hashing is salted by key
exposure logging: recorded once per subject per experiment, idempotent across repeats and concurrency
SQL store: exposures once per unit under concurrency, stitching, stable assignments and analysis
anonymous to user: a visitor keeps the anonymous assignment after signing in, on every device
stable on change: changing weights, traffic or the variant list does not silently reassign exposed subjects
analysis: per-variant exposures, conversions and rates with a two-proportion z-test against control

implementations.notes: Assignments become sticky at expose(); a removed variant reassigns visibly. PGlite tests run on one connection.
